ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — Yul Brynner

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for an itchy rash on pembrolizumab

text.paragraph: Itchy rash on the chest, back, and arms for four days, during pembrolizumab treatment. [S]

Mr. Brynner is a 63-year-old man with stage IVB adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe (PD-L1 70 percent, no actionable alteration) who had his second pembrolizumab infusion one week ago and his first zoledronic acid dose the same day. He asked for a same-day visit for an itchy rash. Four days ago he noticed small red bumps on his chest that have spread to his upper back and the inner arms. The itching is worst at night and in the heat of the stage lights at rehearsal, but he is sleeping. He has had no blisters, peeling, mouth or eye soreness, genital sores, or fever. The aches he had for a day after the zoledronic acid dose have gone. He has started no new soap, detergent, or medicine other than the infusions. He has had no diarrhea, abdominal pain, cough, breathlessness, headache, unusual fatigue, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. His voice remains improved since the injection two weeks ago. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-20; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Discrete and partly joined pink macules and papules over the anterior chest, upper back, and inner upper arms, about 8 percent of body surface area; scratch marks; no blisters, target lesions, skin pain, or peeling; Nikolsky sign negative
Soft and non-tender; no liver enlargement

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, stage IVB (cT4 N2 M1c, AJCC 8th edition), unresectable: the primary invades the mediastinum at the aortopulmonary window; bone metastases; PD-L1 tumor proportion score 70 percent (22C3); ECOG performance status 1; comprehensive genomic profiling results in the notes
S — Synthetic modern histology, stage, and biomarkers linked to his documented inoperable lung cancer of September 1983.
Bone metastases at T10, the right ilium, and the left sixth rib on PET-CT, without pain, fracture, or cord compression
S — Synthetic metastatic sites chosen so that first-line systemic therapy is the standard of care; no source describes the spread of his cancer.
Left vocal fold paralysis with a breathy, weak voice, most likely from left recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement by disease in the aortopulmonary window
S — Synthetic laryngoscopy finding anchored to the published account that a vocal-cord problem led to his diagnosis; the lay 'lump on his vocal cords' is not modeled as a laryngeal tumor.
Left upper lobe mass invading the mediastinum, with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes, on CT at presentation; suspicious for lung cancer pending tissue diagnosis
S — Synthetic presenting imaging finding, recorded before the tissue diagnosis.
Former smoker: about 3 packs a day from age 12 until he quit 12 years ago, roughly 115 pack-years; no tobacco since
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to the documented heavy smoking and quitting; the pack-year figure is a synthetic midpoint of conflicting published amounts.
Immune-related maculopapular rash from pembrolizumab, grade 1 (about 8 percent of body surface area, itchy, no blisters or mucosal involvement)
S — Synthetic common immune-related adverse event on checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

list.item:
Immune-related maculopapular rash, grade 1 (L27.0). Itchy maculopapular rash over less than 10 percent of the body surface, starting three and a half weeks into pembrolizumab, without blisters, mucosal involvement, skin pain, or fever: grade 1 immune-related dermatitis. No feature of a severe cutaneous reaction. TSH 2.6, free T4 1.1, and liver tests and creatinine normal, so no second immune-related event; eosinophils mildly raised at 0.62, typical of a drug-related rash. Zoledronic acid is an unlikely cause. Pembrolizumab can continue. [S]
Triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily for up to two weeks, not on the face or skin folds.
Cetirizine 10 mg daily as needed for itching; fragrance-free emollient twice daily; cool showers.
Continue pembrolizumab on schedule; oncology informed today and agrees.
Return the same day for blisters, skin pain or peeling, mouth or eye sores, fever, or spread to more than a tenth of the body; photograph the rash every two days.

Stage IVB adenocarcinoma of the lung on pembrolizumab (C34.12). Second cycle given one week ago; no other immune-related symptoms. [S]
Cycle 3 in two weeks after the laboratory panel.
Response CT about nine weeks after starting, as planned.

Follow-up: Skin check at the preventive visit next week, or sooner as above. Cycle 3 in two weeks. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-27: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
